title: Talk to the top about their priorities
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What does the person at the top care about?

Jose said that the aim is relevance, clarity, credibility, efficiency and understanding high-level priorities. If you talk about graphic design to a chief executive, he will say talk to my marketing department.
A student said that a chief executive cares about the bottom line, so you connect what you sell to how it affects the bottom line.
Jose played a call as a brainstorm: the reason I am calling is that we serve a lot of major organizations in a sector, and we speak about a problem they share. He said it works in any industry.
Another said that when calling repair shops it is easier to reach the person, though they are very busy, and he would adapt the opening.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the person you want to reach.
Write what they care about most.
Write your opening in two sentences.
Write the problem you both know.

check.q: What did a student say a chief executive cares about?
What did Jose list as the aims?
What did Jose say about the practice call?

recap: Talk about their priorities. Connect to the bottom line.
